title: False friends
what: words that look like a word in another language but mean something else ('actual' for current, 'eventually' for possibly, 'sympathetic' for nice, 'propose' for suggest, 'control' for check)
summary: False friends persist because their similarity to native language words makes them seem correct. This leads to subtle misunderstandings and can undermine the speaker's credibility in professional contexts.
listenFor: Pay close attention to words that sound or look like terms in your native language but might carry different meanings in English.

contrasts.wrong: We will eventually go to the conference next year.
contrasts.right: We will possibly go to the conference next year.
contrasts.note: "Eventually" means in the end; "possibly" means perhaps.

contrasts.wrong: My new colleague is very sympathetic.
contrasts.right: My new colleague is very kind.
contrasts.note: "Sympathetic" means showing understanding; "kind" means friendly or generous.

contrasts.wrong: Please control the documents before sending them.
contrasts.right: Please check the documents before sending them.
contrasts.note: "Control" means to direct or manage; "check" means to verify.

contrasts.wrong: He is very sensible to criticism.
contrasts.right: He is very sensitive to criticism.
contrasts.note: "Sensible" means practical or reasonable; "sensitive" means easily affected.

drills: The current market trends indicate a shift in consumer behavior.
We will possibly need to revise the project timeline.
She is a very kind person, always willing to help others.
I suggest we explore alternative solutions for this challenge.
Please check the figures carefully before submitting the report.
He is quite sensitive to strong opinions during discussions.
The actual cost exceeded our initial projections significantly.
They will eventually reach a consensus after thorough deliberation.
It was a sensible decision to invest in renewable energy sources.
We need to control the budget strictly to avoid overspending.

probes.sentence: He is a very sympathetic manager, always listening.
answers: He is a very understanding manager, always listening.
He is a very friendly manager, always listening.

probes.sentence: Can you control if the data has been updated?
answers: Can you check if the data has been updated?

probes.sentence: Her skin is very sensible to sunlight.
answers: Her skin is very sensitive to sunlight.
